tasks.short: Give the safety instruction for each machine, demonstrate care of tools and materials, monitor students at work, and record who passed the machine instruction.

steps.what: Technical teacher instructs students in the safe use of each machine
Technical teacher demonstrates the care of equipment and materials to prevent damage
Technical teacher monitors students using equipment to prevent injury
Technical teacher records which students passed the machine instruction: on paper lists kept and copied per workshop today, ticked per student in the student system after the change

tasks.design: Machine instruction results are ticked per student in the student system ({OTHER}), which prints a clearance list per workshop and shows it on the teacher's tablet, so paper lists are not kept and copied. Instructing, demonstrating and monitoring stay with the teacher.
tasks.previous_blocker: Clearance lists were kept on paper per workshop.
tasks.enabler_now: Student systems can hold per-student clearances and print lists per room.
tasks.still_hard: A student who passed the instruction can still take shortcuts.
tasks.human_edge: Stopping a student before a hand gets near a blade.

evidence.claim: Student systems can record per-student clearances and print lists per room.

assumptions: Boundary: from the workshop plan to the clearance list; machine maintenance is outside.
Input contract: machine list kept by the workshop assistant; fallback is paper lists.
Instructing and monitoring do not change.
Ticking who passed is a first record and keeps its time; s4 keeps 60 because only keeping, copying and handing round paper lists goes.
research_questions: Are clearance lists current at every lesson?

incremental.description: No new ongoing work for the teacher; the machine list is kept by the workshop assistant.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: one workshop with few machines and one list, so little copying goes and s4 keeps 80 (2.0); high: several workshops sharing the lists (4.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Write objectives for units and projects, put lesson objectives on the slides, publish unit objectives to students, explain objectives at the start of lessons, and check at the end whether they were met.

steps.what: Technical teacher establishes clear objectives for units and projects

loop.input: The exam programme, last year's unit plan and the teacher's notes for changes.
loop.output: Draft objectives for each unit and project in student language.
loop.check: Code checks each objective maps to an exam programme code and every code in scope is covered; the teacher reads each objective against the code's text and the unit's projects and rewrites objectives whose meaning or level is off.
loop.stop: Stops when the checks pass and the teacher approves, or after two failed redrafts the teacher writes them.
loop.why_not_simpler: Objectives must be written in student language per project; the exam programme codes alone are not readable for students.

steps.what: Technical teacher writes lesson objectives on the board and slides
Technical teacher checks the unit objectives before students see them: wording in student language, matching the exam programme and the unit
Technical teacher publishes the checked unit objectives for students: uploaded by hand today, one release in the learning environment after the change
Technical teacher communicates the objectives to students at the start of lessons
Technical teacher checks with students at the end of the lesson whether objectives were met

tasks.design: A bounded step drafts unit and project objectives in student language from the exam programme and last year's plan; code checks every objective maps to an exam programme code, and the teacher edits. Lesson slides pull the day's objectives from the unit plan by template. Once the teacher has checked the final objectives, the teacher publishes them once in the learning environment ({LMS}). Explaining and checking objectives with students stay with the teacher.
tasks.previous_blocker: Objectives were rewritten for each unit and copied onto boards and slides by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Language models draft objectives in plain language; slide templates pull from unit plans.
tasks.still_hard: Students only take objectives seriously when the teacher makes them real.
tasks.human_edge: Linking an objective to a job a student wants.
tasks.altitude: The teacher edits drafted objectives instead of rewriting them.

reach.task: Check coverage of the exam programme

evidence.claim: In a randomised trial with 259 science teachers, ChatGPT plus a guide cut weekly planning from 81.5 to 56.2 minutes with no quality difference.
Drafting objectives is not an Annex III use; AI that evaluates learning outcomes is.

assumptions: Boundary: from the exam programme to objectives checked; assessment is outside.
Input contract: exam programme from the national body; unit plans kept by the section; fallback is writing by hand.
Explaining and checking objectives do not change.
No student data go into the drafting step.
s1 keeps 75 because the teacher reads and rewrites the drafted objectives for meaning; s3 keeps 25 for the release.
research_questions: How much of the drafted objectives does the teacher change?

already_counted.description: Technical teacher edits and approves drafted objectives.

incremental.description: Technical teacher keeps the unit plan template current.

approvals.approved_version: The unit objectives exactly as checked by the teacher in s3b, published once to the students of the named unit in the learning environment; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: new units each year, so drafts and the slide template help less and s1 keeps 90 and s2 keeps 70 (9.5); high: repeat units with small changes (18.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Prepare slides and video clips, set up the projector, sound and demonstration equipment, present with audio-visual aids, and put the slides in the learning environment.

steps.what: Technical teacher prepares slides and video clips for the lesson
Technical teacher sets up the projector, sound and demonstration equipment
Technical teacher uses computers, audio-visual aids and equipment to supplement presentations
Technical teacher checks the slides before students get them: content right for this class, sources credited, nothing that should not be shared
Technical teacher uploads the checked slides to the learning environment: by hand today, one release to the class after the change

tasks.design: The section keeps slides and video clips per topic in a shared library ({DOCS}), so the teacher adapts rather than builds. Workshop classrooms get a fixed screen with one-click casting, so setting up takes less time. Once the teacher has checked the finished slides, the teacher releases them once to the class in the learning environment ({LMS}). Presenting and demonstrating stay with the teacher.
tasks.previous_blocker: Each teacher built slides alone and set up borrowed equipment every lesson.
tasks.enabler_now: Shared libraries and fixed classroom screens are common in schools.
tasks.still_hard: Machines in the workshop still need to be prepared by hand.
tasks.human_edge: Pausing a video at the moment students start asking questions.

reach.learn: Whether the shared library is reused.

evidence.claim: Shared document libraries can hold slides and clips per topic; classroom screens support casting from a laptop.

assumptions: Boundary: from the lesson plan to media published; the school's equipment budget is outside.
Input contract: library kept by the section; fixed screens installed by the school; fallback is building slides alone and borrowed projectors.

incremental.description: Technical teacher adds new slides and clips to the shared library.

approvals.approved_version: The slides exactly as checked by the teacher in s4b, released once to the named class in the learning environment; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: a single teacher per subject with few shared slides and casting not in every room, so s1 keeps 85 and s2 keeps 80 (10.2); high: a section sharing topics (22.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Read the student's results and absence, talk with the student, contact parents, consult the care coordinator, record the talk, and find internships or extra challenges for special interests.

steps.what: Technical teacher reads the student's results and absence before the talk
Technical teacher guides and counsels students with adjustment or academic problems
Technical teacher contacts parents by phone or e-mail
Technical teacher consults the care coordinator
Technical teacher writes the talk notes in the student record
Technical teacher finds internships or extra challenges for students with special interests

tasks.design: A mentor view in the student system ({OTHER}) shows results, absence and earlier talk notes together before a talk. Talk notes use a short template with agreed actions and a follow-up date. Internship places and extra challenges come from the school's internship database, searchable by trade. Counselling the student, contacting parents and consulting the care coordinator stay with the teacher.
tasks.previous_blocker: Results, absence and notes were looked up in several screens and internships found by phone.
tasks.enabler_now: Student systems offer mentor views; schools keep internship databases.
tasks.still_hard: Problems at home rarely show in the data.
tasks.human_edge: Finding the workshop task that makes a struggling student proud.

evidence.claim: Student systems can show results, absence and notes in one mentor view.
Under the WMS, parents and pupils consent to rules on pupil data.

assumptions: Boundary: from the student's concern to the options found; formal care plans are outside.
Input contract: results and absence from the student system; internship database kept by the school; fallback is several screens and phone.
Counselling and contacting parents do not change.
Talk notes are a first record: s5 keeps 85, saving only the layout and standard fields.
research_questions: Do agreed follow-ups happen on time?

incremental.description: No new ongoing work; follow-up dates are part of writing the notes in s5.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few students needing guidance and an incomplete internship database, so s1 and s6 keep 80 (5.5); high: a mentor group with many concerns (9.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The technical teacher keeps instructing safely, explaining objectives, presenting and counselling students; paper lists, rewritten objectives, building slides alone and searching screens shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A teacher with more time in the workshop with students.
